facts.text: There are three exams, each worth 15% (45% total). They test the main theories and concepts from the lectures and textbook, with true/false, multiple-choice and short-answer questions. Exams are held during regular class time.
facts.quote: There will be three close book quizzes to test students' knowledge of the main theories and concepts from the lecture and textbook.

facts.text: Exam note sheet: students may bring one letter-sized sheet of notes, front and back, printed or hand-written. No other materials.
facts.quote: students can prepare and use notes on one piece of paper with two sides permitted (regular letter size)

facts.text: Exam room and timing: 1 hour 15 minutes, 5:30-6:45 pm, JSOM 2.722. No entry allowed after 5:45 pm. Students cannot leave before 5:50 pm.
facts.quote: No entry allowed after 5:45 pm

facts.text: No electronic devices are allowed during exams. Bring a pen (not a pencil, it fades).
facts.quote: No electronic devices will be allowed.

facts.text: Exam 1 format: 45 questions (30 multiple-choice with one answer, 10 true/false, 5 short answer on concepts and explanation). For short answers, clear handwriting matters; exact wording does not, as long as the meaning is the same.
facts.quote: 30 multiple-choice questions (only one answer)

facts.text: Exam 2 format: 45 questions (30 multiple-choice, 10 true/false, 5 short answer: 2 on concepts and explanation, and 3 on comparative advantage, tariff barriers and the prisoner's dilemma).
facts.quote: Comparative advantage/Tariff barriers/Prisoner

facts.text: Exam 3 format: 40 questions (25 multiple-choice, 10 true/false, 4 short answer) plus one comprehensive question on layoff/hiring.
facts.quote: Comprehensive question (layoff/hiring)

facts.text: Make-up exams are only possible in extraordinary situations, with pre-approval at least one week before the exam date. The instructor may not give full credit for a late exam, depending on why the student could not take it.
facts.quote: Make-up quizzes are only possible under extraordinary situations, with pre-approval at least a week prior to the quiz date.

facts.text: Groups sign up in Week 2. Each group has 6 students (some groups may have 5).
facts.quote: Each group will consist of 6 students (certain groups may only have 5 students).

facts.text: Each group picks one real-world multinational corporation (MNC) and writes background research on it, covering areas such as: main business (product/service, industry, mission), history, geographic scope, ownership structure (parent/subsidiaries, public/private, major shareholders), financial performance, key stakeholders (customers, suppliers, employees, competitors), and others.
facts.quote: Each group will select one real-world multinational corporation (MNC) and finish a background research for the MNC.

facts.text: The mid-term report is about 3-6 double-spaced pages, Times New Roman, font size 12. It is worth 10% and is due 10/10 at 11:59 PM.
facts.quote: a written report about 3-6 double-spaced pages (Times New Roman font, font size 12)

facts.text: Building on the mid-term background research, each group analyzes the MNC's international strategy that may explain its success or failure abroad, and develops solutions to its challenges. Possible areas: firm resources and capabilities; formal and informal institutional influences (political, legal, cultural, ethical); international trade and global competitive dynamics; corporate governance and social responsibility; global challenges; market selection and entry mode; alliances and acquisitions; others.
facts.quote: each group needs to conduct further analysis for the MNC to identify its international strategy

facts.text: For each strategy, analyze whether it succeeded or failed. If it succeeded, explain why and its implications. If it failed, give solutions or recommendations.
facts.quote: If you believe a strategy is a success, discuss the reason behind it and its implications.

facts.text: The final project has a written report of about 6-10 double-spaced pages (Times New Roman, size 12) and a group presentation of about 25 minutes to the whole class. Worth 35% in total: presentation 15%, report 20%. The report is due 12/13 at 11:59 PM.
facts.quote: a written report of about 6-10 double-spaced pages

facts.text: Quality matters more than quantity. Long writing without clear logic, objective explanation, analysis and recommendations will not score high. Sub-titles are recommended. Include exhibits and references for information sources.
facts.quote: Please note that quality matters more than quantity.

facts.text: The self and peer evaluation (10%) is anonymous. Names on the form are only used to track scores and are deleted after scoring. A student's score is the average of the scores from all group members and themselves. Due 11/12 at 11:59 PM.
facts.quote: The score for your evaluation would be the average of the scores from all your group members and yourself.

facts.text: Each person is rated 1-5 (1 = strongly disagree, 5 = strongly agree) on three statements: attends classes and group meetings regularly and arrives on time; contributes meaningfully to group discussions and the success of the project; completes group assignments on time and in a quality manner. Column totals are summed.
facts.quote: Attends classes and group meetings regularly and arrives on time.

facts.quote: Late submission of assignments will be downgraded by 10% on the original score every school day.

criteria.name: Analysis of International Strategy
levels: In-depth analysis of international strategies with detailed insights into firm resources, capabilities, institutional influences, etc.
Good analysis, but may lack depth or critical insight in some areas.
General analysis with limited depth or analysis of certain areas.
Shallow or incomplete analysis; lacks critical evaluation of strategies.

criteria.name: Success/Failure Evaluation
levels: Thorough evaluation of each strategy's success or failure with clear reasoning and evidence.
Evaluation is mostly clear, but may miss some key aspects or evidence.
Basic evaluation of success/failure but lacks evidence or clear reasoning.
Evaluation is unclear, unsupported, or missing critical analysis.

criteria.name: Recommendations and Solutions
levels: Well-thought-out, practical, and actionable solutions to challenges/issues.
Practical solutions with minor weaknesses or gaps in reasoning.
Basic solutions with limited practicality or clarity.
Solutions are unclear, unrealistic, or missing entirely.

criteria.name: Quality of Writing
levels: Writing is clear, concise, and well-organized with minimal grammatical errors.
Clear and organized writing with few grammatical errors.
Some clarity or grammatical issues; organization may be weak in places.
Writing is unclear, disorganized, or has numerous grammatical errors.

criteria.name: Depth of Research and Analysis
levels: Demonstrates thorough research with detailed evidence, data, and a wide variety of relevant sources.
Good research with sufficient evidence and reliable sources, though some areas may lack depth.
Limited research or reliance on basic or few sources; analysis is shallow.
Research is lacking or superficial, with minimal use of evidence or sources.

criteria.name: Clarity and Organization
levels: Presentation is well-structured and flows logically; very clear explanations.
Clear structure and logical flow, with minor issues in clarity or transitions.
Some structure or clarity issues; the flow of ideas may be weak at times.
Disorganized, unclear, and difficult to follow.

criteria.name: Engagement and Delivery
levels: Engages the audience effectively with confident and dynamic delivery; good eye contact and body language.
Engages the audience, but delivery may lack dynamism or confidence at times.
Delivery lacks engagement, with minimal audience interaction or body language.
Monotone, disengaged delivery; no audience interaction.

criteria.name: Depth of Analysis
levels: Excellent analysis of international strategy and challenges, covering all relevant aspects.
Good analysis but may lack depth in certain areas or miss minor points.
Basic analysis with limited depth or missing some key points.
Superficial analysis; many key aspects of strategy and challenges are omitted.

criteria.name: Visual Aids/Supporting Materials
levels: Effective, well-designed visual aids (slides, charts, etc.) that complement and enhance the presentation.
Visual aids are clear and relevant but may not fully complement the spoken content.
Visual aids are somewhat relevant, but may be unclear or underused.
Visual aids are poorly designed or not used effectively.

criteria.name: Team Collaboration
levels: All team members contribute equally, and there is smooth collaboration throughout the presentation.
Most team members contribute equally, with minor issues in collaboration.
Some imbalance in team contribution; one or more members dominate.
Unequal participation from team members; lack of cohesion.
